idiom_name: struct per table plus explicit SQL joins (sqlite3 / libpq)
implementation_notes: C has no inheritance, so the hierarchy becomes record types that share a key: one struct for the base table carrying the key and the type code, one struct per subclass table, and the join is written out in SQL for each read. What replaces the classic mapper is a pair of functions per class - one that loads base plus subclass columns with an INNER JOIN on the shared id, one that inserts into both tables inside a transaction - while polymorphic handling is a switch on the type code, not dispatch. The hand-written form stays justified whenever the schema is fixed (legacy or DBA-owned) or one small subtype is being added to an otherwise flat application.
pitfalls: The two inserts must share one transaction; a failure between them leaves a base row with no subclass row, and SQLite/Postgres will happily keep it.
A query that selects base columns only and then reads subclass fields returns garbage or NULL instead of failing, so every loader must join the full path.
SQLite's flexible typing accepts a mismatched or NULL key where Postgres would reject it; declare the key columns with the same type in both tables.
